scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

This narrative explicitly covers colonial and independent modern Algeria, associated with the 1900 to 1938 algeria record and the algeria-1960 record continuing to the present. These are linked periods, not an assertion of unchanged sovereignty. The precolonial Regency of Algiers remains a separate subject.

The 1900 imported polygon is narrower than later snapshots; the later territory extends deeply into the Sahara. A modern border is not projected backward as the boundary of every community, and imported geometry remains unverified.

The imported algeria-1960 record begins before independence. July 1962 independence is stated separately; no false independence date of 1960 is created. The gap after 1938 is incomplete map coverage, not a historical extinction.

The US diplomatic summary compresses the conquest into 1830. The card says conquest began then and does not claim all resistance or regional autonomy immediately ended. The Crémieux decree is not extended without qualification to every Saharan Jewish community.

The two migration-museum pages are distinct exhibition and thematic accounts. Their derived prose remains conservative. The Messaoudi caption establishes the people, shop, place and decade; it is not used for unsupported visual or demographic deductions.

M’Zab, Touat, Tidikelt and Tlemcen are distinct places and communities. UNESCO statements about M’Zab’s centuries of continuity are not repeated as proof of an entirely unchanging society. Undated practices receive no invented ancient date.

UNESCO inscription dates identify heritage recognition, not origins. Couscous is explicitly shared across four nominating states. The Tlemcen narrative does not turn beliefs about protection into empirically established effects.

Baya’s work is attributed to her own practice rather than a speculative influence on Picasso. The IMA’s full exhibition text was read, including Anissa Bouayed’s account. The complete paid catalog was not read, and no individual painting is given an invented title or date.

Djebar’s Académie biography supports her research among women, the film’s languages and its documented screenings. A semi-documentary film is not treated as unedited testimony or the single account of every woman’s wartime experience.

Human Rights Watch research methods, political-setting section and the Fouad Lakel case were read. The report distinguishes state disappearances from armed-group abductions and notes limits on field access. Allegations and family testimony are attributed, numerical totals omitted, and no 2003 finding is asserted as a current case outcome.

The 2003 period boundary marks the dated investigation and subsequent documentation theme. It is not a claimed end of conflict. The card’s heritage examples do not certify political reform or human-rights compliance.

The Évian source is the diplomatic archives’ description of its 2022 edition, not a claim to have read all negotiation transcripts. March agreement, July referendum and recognition, and October UN membership are distinct.
Independent historical review, border assessment and depth certification remain pending.
